attribution.note: Marcus restates his own 2022 argument in his own post and plainly stands by it. That makes it his claim, not someone else's that he is quoting.

semantics.note: The wording is firm ('would not get us to AGI'), with no hedge and no deadline. The normalised wording keeps both parts: LLMs won't reach AGI, and a new paradigm is needed. Calling it an indefinite forecast is fair. It is recounted from 2022 and reaffirmed in 2023.

contract.note: The plain reading of AGI and of the LLM approach is ordinary and not stretched either way. The bar is equally high for both outcomes: support needs a shown necessity, and contradiction needs an independently verified AGI built within the LLM paradigm. The result still depends on where the paradigm boundary is drawn, and Marcus did not define that.

evidence.note: ARC Prize independently measured strong ARC-AGI-3 results for Astra (Sep 2026), but says outright that the benchmark does not establish AGI. It says nothing about whether a new paradigm was needed.

The AGI Society assessment (Sep 2026, before the cutoff) finds the published evidence does not yet support calling Astra AGI. That rules out contradiction for now, but it does not show LLMs can never reach AGI.
An Oct 2026 preprint reports strong embodied competence with practical gaps remaining. It shows neither AGI nor an inherent limit of the LLM paradigm.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet shows big capability gains (GPT-6 Astra), but independent assessments say AGI has not been shown, so the contradiction condition is not met. Nothing in the packet shows an inherent LLM limit that requires a new paradigm, so the support condition is not met either. Evidence available by the cutoff does not settle the claim.
